title: ARIMA
description: Classical statistical forecasting model combining auto-regressive, moving average, and differencing parameters.
name: ARIMA
summary: ARIMA (AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average) is a generalized statistical model for analyzing and forecasting univariate time series data. It captures temporal structures like trends, autocorrelation, and seasonal variations.
use_when: Forecasting univariate metrics with clear historical trends and stable stationarity.
avoid_when: Working with highly multi-variate sequences or long-term forecasting with non-stationary dynamics.
pros: Well-founded statistical theory with complete confidence interval estimates.
Requires very small amounts of historical training data to fit parameters.
Highly interpretable parameters showing specific seasonal and trend influences.
cons: Limited to univariate sequences by default (requires ARIMAX for exogenous factors).
Poor handling of non-linear patterns or sudden structural breaks in sequences.
Requires manual stationarity checks and parameter search (p, d, q).

key_hyperparams.name: order
key_hyperparams.note: Tuple representing (p, d, q) for autoregressive, integration, and moving average components.

quick_start:
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA
import numpy as np

data = np.random.randn(100).cumsum()
model = ARIMA(data, order=(1,1,1))
model_fit = model.fit()
forecast = model_fit.forecast(steps=5)
